scope: Local GALX SDK/function transport implementation and both runtime replacements; no serving activation
revisionScope: Working tree with exact source hashes below; not yet committed
behavior: SDK automatically executes registered real callbacks and supplies their results to subsequent model steps in run and stream.
Both pool contracts transport bounded function definitions and correlated results; complete successful output calls are rebuilt through explicit nested allowlists.
Invalid arguments produce fixed tool errors for correction without execution; duplicate IDs reject a complete batch; abort prevents future model/callback starts.
Provider-hosted and approval output types fail closed, partial argument deltas are never text, and function requests do not use legacy upstream retries.

checks.result: Compiled private-marker/runtime-trace checks clean; first full command also reported expected stale guide/registry fingerprints pending explicit semantic review.

exploratoryScan: A broader search also matched the existing public Supabase Auth origin in a browser chunk. Inspection identified public client configuration, not new function metadata; no global project-identifier absence claim or scan ignore was introduced.

localAcceptance.scope: local VM separation on one trusted Mac; no provider generation or cloud deployment

installation.workflow: Built both final tools-20260915 images, inspected and loaded each into its own VM; updated manifest and installed overlay; confirmed zero accounts and closed execution; stopped only both runtime containers; normal up waited for central ownership handoff; inspected actual running image IDs and retained state mounts; passed 69 checks.

rollback: Restore Premium candidate-20260915 and Standard recovery-20260915 own-pool pins with execution closed. Reinstall overlay, preserve state and ownership waits, restore compatible caller behavior and requalify. No quota reset, cross-pool transfer or replay of unknown work.

research.use: Application-owned function execution, matching call/output IDs, automatic continuation and explicit strict false for optional Chat-style parameters.
Distinguish Codex thread/turn approvals from the active Responses relay; no app-server approval responder or application permission modification was added.

limits: No real provider sign-in, quota spend or function/image/Sites generation was performed. Synthetic provider acceptance and empty-pool local checks do not establish real account capability.

Callbacks execute in the application consuming the SDK, never on the relay host. Registration authorizes only those callbacks; owner checks and any external application approval requirements remain the caller responsibility.

Only GALX automatic function execution and model continuation were changed. The active Responses transport does not use Codex app-server approval requests; Codex application, managed sandbox and global approval settings were not changed.
The default remains ten model steps, including final synthesis. Positive maxSteps and AbortSignal control duration; no unlimited loop or automatic retry of uncertain work is provided.

Duplicate call IDs are blocked within a run and supplied history. New IDs are new actions; callback side effects need domain idempotency. Restarting an SDK process has no durable exactly-once callback guarantee.
Executable safeParse schemas validate locally when supplied. Plain JSON schemas constrain the provider request but do not themselves implement local callback validation.
Both relays accept client-owned functions as text inference. Standard still rejects Sites, images and provider-hosted tools; cross-pool discovery, fallback and credentials remain prohibited.

Both runtime images were replaced locally with execution closed, preserving named state volumes and central ownership waits. Central and monitor images, database schema, assignments, quotas and activation flags were unchanged.
The workspace SDK source is updated; no external SDK package was published and no public application or cloud runtime was deployed.
The compiled scan covered 669 browser/rendered assets and named private markers. It is not live authenticated UI acceptance or a claim that every public configuration identifier is absent.
